steps.title: Battery & storage habits

steps.description: Use a maintainer if it sits. Clean terminals. Modern AGM vs flooded — match the charger. Parasitic drains on modified radios are common.

risk_confirm.title: Brake failure / contamination risk
risk_confirm.body: Aged hoses, seized calipers, or incorrect fluid can cause brake loss. Some older friction materials may contain asbestos — do not blow dust; use proper shop methods. When unsure, find a nearby shop.

steps.title: Aged brakes — inspect, don't gamble
steps.coach_encourage: Rubber fails quietly until it doesn't. Look at you — about 57% complete.
steps.personalize: Brake safety for your {{year}} {{make}} at {{mileage}} miles.
steps.description: Check pedal firmness, fluid condition (dark = service), hoses for cracks, and parking brake. Many classics need a full hydraulic refresh — that's shop territory if you're unsure.

steps.title: Tires & aged rubber
steps.coach_encourage: Date codes matter more than tread sometimes. You're more than halfway — keep that steady pace.
steps.personalize: Rubber age check on {{model}} at {{mileage}} miles.
steps.description: Read DOT date codes — replace old tires even with tread left. Inspect belts, radiator hoses, and fuel lines for cracks.

steps.title: Rust, frame & floors
steps.coach_encourage: Surface rust vs structural rust — know the difference. Almost there — about 86% through.
steps.description: Check rockers, floors, frame rails, and mount points. Soft floors or perforated rails need a body/frame pro — not bondo over holes.
